sources.title: The Republic of Suriname’s First National Adaptation Plan Progress Report
sources.organization: Ministry of Spatial Planning and Environment, Republic of Suriname
sources.temporal_coverage: Reviews national adaptation progress for 2020-2024; report published 1 April 2025.
sources.methodology: NAP implementation reviewed against indicators using questionnaires, focus groups, interviews and a validation workshop.
sources.limitations: Some indicator data were unavailable; the report is not an impact evaluation.

sources.title: Suriname Systematic Country Diagnostic
sources.temporal_coverage: Diagnostic drafted mainly in 2023; includes 2022 flood observations and a 2023 household phone survey.
sources.methodology: World Bank diagnostic based on two 2022 country visits, stakeholder interviews, literature review and a household phone survey.
sources.limitations: The report cautions that some conditions may have changed since drafting; flood and land-rights sections synthesize earlier sources.

sources.title: Climate Resilience for Food Security in Suriname
sources.organization: Inter-American Institute for Cooperation on Agriculture (IICA), Water and Agriculture platform
sources.temporal_coverage: Project listing states implementation from 2023 to 2024 and finalized status.
sources.methodology: IICA implementer account of field assessments, farmer meetings, demonstration plots and project lessons.
sources.limitations: Project-page account is not an independent evaluation and provides no controlled outcome estimate.

sources.title: Building Indigenous Maroon Farmers’ Resilience to Climate Change Guaranteeing Food Security in Suriname
sources.organization: Inter-American Institute for Cooperation on Agriculture (IICA)
sources.temporal_coverage: Project listing states dates 8 May 2025 to 30 June 2026; current implementation status is not stated.
sources.methodology: IICA project listing summarizing the problem statement, planned training and demonstration-site activities.
sources.limitations: The page states intended activities, not completed outcomes; it does not name participating villages.

claims.locator: Executive summary, PDF p. 2; section 3, table on progress and stakeholder participation, PDF pp. 20-22.
claims.paraphrase: The review reports no formal NAP coordinator, low awareness and financial, staffing and technical constraints; Indigenous and Maroon groups were not consistently included in decisions.
institutions: Ministry of Spatial Planning and Environment
claims.limitations: Not a causal evaluation of resilience effects.

claims.locator: Water-sector progress table, PDF p. 31, item on 2022 EnGenDER project.
claims.paraphrase: In 2022, EnGenDER provided 95 water tanks to three Indigenous and 34 tribal communities in Brokopondo and Sipaliwini districts; Klaaskreek also received water-system rehabilitation.
claims.limitations: The progress report gives aggregate community coverage, not site-level distribution or independent outcome measurement.

claims.locator: Water-sector progress table, PDF p. 30, IICA project completed October 2024.
claims.paraphrase: An IICA project installed low-cost rainwater systems at selected households in Matta and Singri Lanti (Para District) and Tamarin (Marowijne District) to expand potable-water storage.
institutions: Australian High Commission Direct Aid Program
claims.limitations: The reported installations were selected-household outputs; effects on water-borne illness are not evaluated.

claims.locator: Education-sector progress table, PDF p. 58, paragraph on schools in the interior.
claims.paraphrase: The report says schools near riverbeds in Boven-Suriname and Marowijne are considered for relocation from flood-prone sites, but greater distance may impede pupil and teacher access.
institutions: Ministry of Education, Science and Culture
claims.limitations: Relocation is under consideration, not reported as completed; the report gives no school or population counts.

claims.locator: Section 6.2, PDF p. 76, paragraphs on the 2022 floods and southern transport routes.
claims.paraphrase: Heavy rains in March 2022 flooded Brokopondo and other interior districts; reported effects included crop losses, hunger and nearly 1,500 displaced people, while flooded southern roads challenged relief access.
claims.limitations: The SCD summarizes reports from the 2022 event; it does not provide comparable district impact totals.

claims.locator: Section 6.2 and figure 16, PDF pp. 76-77, World Bank 2023 phone-survey findings.
claims.paraphrase: In the 2023 phone survey, 61% of households reported extreme rainfall as a threat, 41% reported flood threat, and 57% were unprepared for disasters; unpreparedness was 64% for female-headed versus 59% for male-headed households.
claims.limitations: The diagnostic reports phone-survey shares but the cited passage does not give sample size or district breakdown.

claims.locator: Section 6.1, PDF p. 75, paragraphs on Indigenous and Maroon land rights and forest management.
claims.paraphrase: The SCD describes long-standing contention and conflicting state-community land claims in the interior involving Indigenous and Maroon communities; natural-resource wealth complicates the rights debate.
claims.limitations: This is FCV-relevant land-rights context; the SCD does not attribute these tensions to climate hazards.

claims.locator: Project lessons, paragraphs on shifting cultivation, demonstration plots and results, webpage paragraphs 2-4.
claims.paraphrase: IICA reports that micro-sprinkler plots improved farmers’ use and scheduling of irrigation water, reducing water loss in its interior farming project.
claims.limitations: Implementer-reported project lesson; the page gives no measured water-saving quantity or comparison group.

claims.locator: Project lessons, paragraphs on the crop nursery and recovered planting material, webpage paragraph 4.
claims.paraphrase: IICA says a crop nursery contributed to recovering bitter cassava and brown upland-rice varieties that had been lost following drought and flooding.
claims.limitations: The page reports a project contribution without naming villages or estimating food-security effects.

claims.paraphrase: IICA’s 2025 project listing says remote Maroon farms face crop-production losses from increasingly frequent extreme rainfall and drought, alongside constrained tools, resources and technical knowledge.
claims.limitations: The listing gives no village names, crop-loss estimates or independent verification of the described trend.

claims.locator: Specific objectives and expected results, project listing paragraphs 3-5.
claims.paraphrase: The project planned farmer training and two micro-irrigated multi-crop plots plus a nursery to strengthen Maroon farmers’ climate-smart production skills.
claims.limitations: These were planned outputs for a project whose stated end date has passed; completion and outcomes are not documented on the page.

access_audit.locator: Full 95-page progress report; implementation methodology, water, education and participation sections.
access_audit.notes: Full report was read. Ministry is identified as publisher; NAP Global Network page states the report date and assessment method.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No separate reuse terms verified; license status remains unknown.

access_audit.locator: Full 104-page SCD; section 6.1 land rights/forest management and section 6.2 flood and disaster-risk discussion, PDF pp. 75-77.
access_audit.notes: Full World Bank diagnostic was read; it states that the core was drafted in Q1 2023 and some conditions may have changed.
access_audit.reuse_terms: World Bank attribution terms apply; no separate open license was verified.

access_audit.locator: Full IICA project page; project status, field lessons and descriptions of irrigation, crop nursery and recovered planting material.
access_audit.notes: The page reports project status as finalized and dates it 2023-2024; findings are implementer-reported.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No separate reuse terms verified; license status remains unknown.

access_audit.locator: Full project listing; problem description, dates, objectives and expected results.
access_audit.notes: The listing gives a 30 June 2026 end date but no completion status or outcome report; it was accessed after that date.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No separate reuse terms verified; license status remains unknown.

access_audit.locator: IDB State of the Climate Report: Suriname, 2021.
access_audit.notes: Direct PDF access exceeded the web reader's 10 MB content limit. No claims rely on indexed text from that report.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Not assessed because the report was not accessed.

search_audit.query: Suriname climate change vulnerability interior Indigenous Maroon villages flood drought named districts official World Bank report
search_audit.outcome: Found the 2022 flood account in Brokopondo and interior districts, the NAP’s named water-system projects and school siting concerns, plus remote Maroon farming vulnerability and project records.

search_audit.query: Suriname climate variability climate change resource competition conflict Indigenous Maroon communities land tenure water report
search_audit.outcome: The SCD describes longstanding Indigenous/Maroon land-right contention and conflicting community/state claims over interior land, with natural-resource wealth complicating reform; it does not link these tensions causally to climate hazards.

search_audit.query: Suriname climate adaptation project implementation barriers conflict insecurity land tenure indigenous communities report
search_audit.outcome: No inspected source reported violence or insecurity disrupting a named climate-adaptation project. The SCD says 2022 flood-damaged roads challenged relief access, a hazard-access effect rather than an FCV constraint.

search_audit.query: Suriname climate resilience adaptation outcomes evaluation indigenous Maroon communities traditional knowledge food water primary report
search_audit.outcome: Found a government NAP review documenting completed water-storage measures and ongoing inclusion/coordination gaps, alongside IICA-reported irrigation and crop-nursery results and a separate 2025-2026 planned Maroon farmer initiative.

gaps: No inspected primary source demonstrated a climate-to-conflict causal pathway or violence/insecurity constraining adaptation delivery. Interior land-rights contention is relevant context but is not linked by the SCD to climate hazards.
The NAP progress report relies on stakeholder reporting and notes missing indicator information; its activities and outputs are not an independent impact evaluation.
The World Bank SCD draws on 2022 consultations and a 2023 phone survey, and warns that some conditions may have changed since the report was drafted.
IICA's finalized 2023-2024 project results are implementer-reported, without an independent counterfactual or quantified food-security effect.
The IICA 2025-2026 project listing was accessed after its stated end date but does not say whether planned activities were completed.
The IDB State of the Climate PDF exceeded the web reader's 10 MB limit and was not used; recent, district-disaggregated hazard and preparedness evidence remains limited.
